history.dynasty: Gelugpa order of Tibetan Buddhism (monastery tradition)
history.period: Site associated with the 8th century CE; present monastery structure established 1684 (sources also report 1860-61 - unverified)
history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - Tibetan Buddhist monastery and sacred site perched on a cliffside in Tawang district, kept for keep-or-drop decision. The site is believed to have been consecrated by Guru Padmasambhava in the 8th century CE; the present monastery was established in 1684 and has three tiers, each dedicated to a Tibetan guru or god. It lies about 45 km from Tawang town, 5 km from Madhuri Lake (Sangester Lake), with a meditation cave of the Guru behind the main complex. Coordinates are from a geocoder POI match (Taktsang Gompa, Zemithang) and are approximate (verify).

name: Tawang Taktshang Monastery
town_description: Tawang is a Himalayan town at about 3,048 m in western Arunachal Pradesh, home to the Monpa tribe and the 400-year-old Tawang Monastery - India's largest Buddhist monastery. Set near the India-Bhutan-Tibet trijunction, it is reached via the Sela Pass and draws pilgrims, trekkers and travellers to its lakes, war memorial and monasteries.

travel.airport: Salonibari Airport, Tezpur (about 318-350 km away); helicopter services from Tezpur and Guwahati are reported
travel.railway: Nearest railhead Bhalukpong (about 280 km away); Tezpur/Rangapara stations also used
travel.road: Tawang is reached by road via NH-13 over the Sela Pass from Bomdila/Tezpur/Guwahati; the monastery is about 45 km from Tawang town, a 5 km drive from Madhuri Lake
